subject: OrbitBank: unexpected throttling affecting reserved throughput
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@orbitbank.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@orbitbank.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Persistent 429s and 5x latency on payments inference (OrbitBank)

Diego —

We started seeing a sharp increase in latency and 429 responses on our payments pipeline last night (~22:30 PST). Impact: intermittent failures for authorization checks which touch your dedicated pool (ORBIT-dedicated-1). Traffic volume has not increased on our side.

Attached: orbitbank_prefix_latency_log.zip (sample traces) and a CSV of hour-by-hour error rates.

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether reserved throughput is being honored for our contract? This is blocking transactions and we've opened an internal incident. If you can join a quick bridge (we're available now) that would be ideal.

Samir Khan
Head of Platform, OrbitBank
samir.k@orbitbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OrbitBank incident — internal triage notes

Internal only — preliminary findings from ops triage (do not forward to customer yet):

Summary:
- Root cause candidate: a maintenance job (garbage collection of stale KV cache entries) ran on the serving cluster that inadvertently pinned GPUs used by a handful of background retraining tasks. Those retrain jobs repeatedly requeued and caused placement pressure in the dedicated pool serving OrbitBank.
- Effect: contention on reserved nodes led to queuing and token-generation timeouts, resulting in 429s and visible latency spikes.

Actions taken (short term):
1) Isolated and terminated the rogue retrain jobs that were consuming GPUs.
2) Forced eviction of background workloads from the OrbitBank pool and added two reserved nodes from our regional buffer to reduce queueing (temporary reassign).
3) Enabled aggressive prefix/KV cache bypass for OrbitBank for the next 12 hours to reduce memory pressure.

Customer impact: partial mitigation in place; error rate dropped from ~6.4% to ~1.1% in the last 40 minutes but latency is still elevated (~2.2x).

Next steps (owner):
- Rishi: finalize node rebalancing and verify long-lived job isolation + add a restrictive label to prevent future placement (ETA 3 hours).
- Vivek: prepare an incident note and draft customer-facing language; coordinate credit discussion with Lauren.
- Diego: set up exec sync if OrbitBank requests one; coordinate with Sales for any SLA concessions.

Notes: we'll need to decide whether to offer a one-off reserved-throughput credit vs. a service credit under the SLA. Recommend documenting the root cause and the mitigation timeline before proposing credits.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: provisioning-runbook.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2027 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OrbitBank incident — engineer runbook & mitigation commands

Following up with technical remediation steps and verification commands we executed:

Steps executed:
- kubectl -n serving scale nodepool-orbitbank --replicas=6  # temporarily increased reserved nodes
- systemctl stop retrain-worker@{12..18}  # terminated retrain workers causing contention
- Apply placement label: kubectl label nodes orbit-* prevent-background=true
- Deployed a model-variant fallback for heavy requests: model=paylite-quant-v2 (smaller KV footprint)

Verification:
- Observed queue depth drop from 42 -> 3 over 35 minutes.
- 95th percentile latency improved from 1.9s -> 0.95s for short requests; long-tail still at 1.6s (target 0.7s).

Longer term items (RFCs to follow):
- Auto-isolation for reserved pools when background maintenance jobs are scheduled.
- Stronger gating on batch retrain scheduling in production clusters.
- Add a soft reservation that prevents eviction of reserved pool nodes without explicit approval.

I'll continue to monitor; next check-in at 14:00 PST.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

Attachments: orbitbank_prefix_latency_log.zip

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@orbitbank.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@orbitbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: OrbitBank incident update and next steps (resolved -> monitoring)

Samir / Priya —

Thank you for your patience. Summary of what happened and what we did:

- Incident: background maintenance and retrain jobs caused resource contention on the region serving cluster, which partially consumed reserved nodes for ORBIT-dedicated-1 and produced queuing/429s.
- Immediate mitigation: evicted background workloads, increased temporary node count for the OrbitBank pool, and enabled a smaller model variant for heavy requests.
- Current status: error rate has returned to baseline (~0.2%), 95th percentile latency is ~0.75s (within SLA targets for committed throughput).

Short-term commitments:
- We'll keep the temporary node reassignments for 48 hours while we validate stability.
- We're scheduling a joint post-incident review (technical) with OrbitBank engineers for next week; proposed slots: Mon 2/15 or Tue 2/16.
- We'll propose a one-time service credit for the measurable downtime window; Lauren is looping with finance/sales to finalize the amount and will follow up.

Long-term changes planned:
- Auto-isolation of reserved pools during scheduled maintenance.
- Placement policy changes to prevent retrain jobs from landing on reserved nodes.
- Enhanced alerting for early queue growth detection and preemptive autoscaling.

If you'd like an executive-level call to discuss org impact or compensation, I'm happy to arrange it — otherwise we'll run the post-mortem and share the findings.

Apologies again for the disruption. We're committed to preventing recurrence.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.ai
